## Key facts about painting in Denver, Colorado

These are the substantive, verifiable points covered on the site.

### Why exterior paint fails faster at altitude

Denver sits at 5,280 feet above sea level. The U.S. Environmental Protection
Agency reports that ultraviolet radiation increases by approximately two percent
for every 1,000 feet of elevation gain. UV breaks down the resin binder that
holds pigment to siding, which produces chalking, fading and eventually peeling.
Colorado's UV Index routinely reaches the "very high" and "extreme" ranges on the
EPA scale, including on cool and partly cloudy days.

South-facing and west-facing walls receive substantially more UV exposure than
north-facing walls and typically show wear first.

### Freeze-thaw damage

Denver commonly experiences temperature swings of forty degrees or more within a
single day during spring and fall. These swings cause siding to expand and
contract repeatedly. Moisture that penetrates a hairline crack freezes, expands,
and pushes the coating away from the substrate from underneath. This makes caulk
inspection at every joint a critical prep step in this market.

### Hail

Colorado, Nebraska and Wyoming form the region the National Weather Service
refers to as Hail Alley, the most hail-prone area of the United States. Hail
chips coating from the exposed edges of lap siding and drives moisture into the
wood underneath, where it can cause rot before the damage becomes visible from
ground level.

### Best time of year to paint exteriors in Denver

May through September is the most reliable window. Late April and October are
strong shoulder periods that are frequently overlooked; cooler surface
temperatures hold a longer wet edge and produce a more uniform finish than
painting in direct afternoon sun. The limiting factor in Denver is usually the
overnight low rather than the daytime high, because most exterior products
require surface temperatures above roughly 50 degrees Fahrenheit through cure.
July and August require scheduling around the afternoon thunderstorm pattern.
November through March is best suited to interior, cabinet and commercial work.

### Signs an exterior is due for repainting

Chalking (white powder transfers to a dark cloth rubbed on the siding), uneven
fade between sun-exposed and shaded walls, caulk pulling away from joints,
peeling or blistering, exposed bare wood, and hail chipping along lap siding
edges. Any two occurring together indicate the surface is due.

### What proper exterior prep includes

Pressure washing to remove dust and chalked coating; scraping failed paint back
to a sound edge and feathering the transition; wood rot repair and board
replacement; full caulk inspection at every joint where two materials meet;
priming of bare substrate, patched areas and severe color changes. Prep is
typically the largest labor line on a correctly written exterior estimate.

### What drives painting cost in Denver

Square footage and number of stories; substrate type (wood, fiber cement, vinyl,
stucco, brick, each requiring different primers and prep); the condition of the
existing coating, which is the largest single swing factor; number of colors in
the scheme; product grade; depth of prep required; and for interiors, ceiling
height, texture matching and trim linear footage.

### Research on paint and home sale price

Zillow's Paint Colors Analysis reviewed more than 32,000 photos from listings
that sold nationally, controlling for square footage, home age, transaction date
and location. Homes with exteriors in "greige" (a blend of light gray and beige)
sold for approximately $3,496 more than comparable homes painted medium brown or
finished in tan stucco. Front doors in dark navy through slate gray were
associated with roughly $1,514 more at closing. A later expansion analyzed more
than 135,000 listing photos from sales between 2010 and 2018.

Zillow's more recent buyer research found sage green was the only shade to rank
in the top tier across every room tested, while a bold red bathroom drew offers
approximately $7,971 lower than the same room in white.

These figures are national averages reflecting correlation across large samples,
not guarantees for any individual property.

### HOA considerations

A large share of Denver metro homes are located within homeowners associations
that maintain approved exterior color palettes. Color approval should be
confirmed before work begins. Portions of Denver also fall within designated
historic districts where exterior changes may require review.

### Pre-1978 homes

Homes built before 1978 may contain lead paint, which affects how disturbed
surfaces must be handled. Older Denver neighborhoods including Washington Park,
Congress Park, Baker, Platt Park, Berkeley, Sunnyside, Whittier, Five Points and
Park Hill contain substantial pre-1978 housing stock.
